trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability shift coincides with a real macro catalyst (jobs data, credit event, geopolitical shock) or is just thin-market noise on Polymarket.
time_plan.1h: Compare against front-end rates (2Y yield, SOFR futures) to confirm the easing signal is corroborated by liquid rate markets.
time_plan.2h: Recheck TLT price vs. move in 2Y/10Y yields; if TLT hasn't followed rate futures, treat the signal as weak.
time_plan.6h: Assess whether any Fed speak or data release explains the move and whether it is already public.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate net TLT move vs. predicted range; log whether the prediction-market shift led or lagged the bond move.

predictions.reasoning: A market on 10 Fed cuts (~250bps) in 2026 is a deep-recession/emergency-easing tail scenario. A sharp rise in its implied probability would signal expectations of aggressive front-loaded easing, which pushes the front end and long-end Treasury yields lower and TLT higher. But because 10 cuts is an extreme strike with tiny baseline odds, even a notable probability jump translates into only a modest, noisy duration move over 12h.

predictions.reasoning: Aggressive expected Fed easing narrows rate differentials and typically weakens the dollar. If the 10-cut probability spikes, it implies a dovish/crisis repricing that would pressure USD lower. However, a recession-driven easing scenario can also trigger safe-haven USD demand, making the net direction ambiguous and the magnitude small.

evidence_used: Market question implies 10x 25bp cuts (~250bps) in 2026, a deep-easing tail scenario
Rate-cut expectations map to Treasury duration (TLT) and USD via rate differentials
Extreme strike means low baseline probability and high noise sensitivity
Category tags (military_conflict) appear mislabeled and unreliable
uncertainty_notes: 10 cuts is an extreme tail; probability moves are likely dominated by thin-market noise rather than real information
The 700bps tradable threshold is far above realistic 12h moves for these liquid proxies, so neither prediction is tradable
Recession-driven easing can produce conflicting USD signals (dovish vs. safe-haven)
No clear geopolitical/macro catalyst is given, so directionality is speculative

llm_justification.summary: The market asks about an extreme 10-cut (~250bps) Fed easing scenario in 2026. A sharp rise in its implied probability would signal expectations of deep recession or emergency easing, favoring long-duration Treasuries (TLT up) and a softer dollar (UUP down). But this is a tail strike with tiny baseline odds, so probability shifts are dominated by thin-market noise, mappings are weak, and expected 12h magnitudes (~25-40bps) fall far below the 700bps tradable threshold. Treat as low-confidence research signal, not tradable.
key_assumptions: A rising 10-cut probability reflects genuine dovish/recession repricing rather than illiquid-market noise
Rate-cut expectations transmit to Treasury duration and USD through standard rate-differential channels
The move is not already fully reflected in liquid rate and FX markets
failure_modes: The Polymarket move is thin-market noise with no macro information content
Recession fears trigger safe-haven USD strength, reversing the UUP thesis
Signal was already public via rate futures, so no leading information
10-cut strike is so extreme that its probability barely moves and carries no exploitable signal
Proxies (TLT, UUP) respond to many drivers unrelated to a single tail rate-path market
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
